title: Decision Prover — Evaluation Battery
note_to_candidate: This file is the input to your system. For each decision, your system must emit a verdict (SUPPORTED | REFUTED | UNDECIDABLE) together with an auditable derivation, the binding constraints it checked, the load-bearing assumptions it relied on, and an attempted refutation. Do NOT hardcode to these items — we will also run held-out decisions you have not seen. All monetary values are USD. 'mo' = per month.

verdict_definitions.SUPPORTED: There exists a valid derivation, from the stated facts and assumptions, showing the decision satisfies every hard constraint AND meets its stated objective. No hard constraint is violated under the decision's own stated assumptions.
verdict_definitions.REFUTED: The decision provably violates at least one hard constraint, OR its negation is provable (an available alternative strictly dominates it on the stated objective), given the facts and assumptions.
verdict_definitions.UNDECIDABLE: The verdict depends on a load-bearing assumption whose truth value is NOT pinned down by the stated facts — the decision is SUPPORTED under one reading of that assumption and REFUTED under another. The honest output names the pivotal assumption (and, ideally, the threshold at which the verdict flips) and declines to assert a proof.
verdict_definitions.precedence_rule: A hard-constraint violation REFUTES a decision regardless of how attractive its projected returns are. Check feasibility before optimality.

schema.decision: id, company, proposal(prose), action(structured), objective(what 'good' means here), stated_assumptions[{id,statement,status:'given'|'projected'}]
schema.expected_output_per_decision: classification, derivation[ordered steps: {rule, inputs, result}], binding_constraints[{id, pass|fail, why}], load_bearing_assumptions[], refutation{attempted, failure_conditions}, for_UNDECIDABLE:{pivotal_assumption, flip_threshold}

constraints.statement: Cash balance must never fall below the $500,000 operating reserve.
At least 6 months of forward runway must be MAINTAINED at all times.
constraints.note: board mandate; this is a maintained invariant, not a one-time check

constraints.statement: Any single new initiative's budget must be <= $1,500,000.
A growth channel may only be scaled if its LTV/CAC >= 3.0.

backlog_units.note: non-cancellable, 30% deposit already taken; contractually due within 6 months

demand_status.note: existing backlog plus inbound orders already exceed what the line can build

constraints.statement: Cash balance must never fall below $1,000,000.
Any single new initiative's budget must be <= $2,000,000.
The 200-unit backlog must be delivered within 6 months (penalty clauses on late delivery).
constraints.note: check whether a decision makes this satisfiable or unsatisfiable

net_income_monthly.note: company is profitable; runway is not a binding concern

constraints.statement: Any new SKU must clear a 25% contribution-margin hurdle.
Any single new initiative's budget must be <= $3,000,000.
Total marketing spend must be <= 12% of revenue.

decisions.proposal: Hire 5 additional engineers immediately to accelerate the roadmap.
decisions.objective: Increase product velocity while remaining within all hard constraints.

decisions.proposal: Run a paid-acquisition test with a $300,000 budget. Projected channel CAC is $5,000; acquired customers are projected to behave like the current cohort.
decisions.objective: Discover a scalable acquisition channel without endangering the balance sheet.

stated_assumptions.statement: Projected CAC for the channel is approximately $5,000.
Acquired customers churn and monetize like the existing cohort.

decisions.proposal: Acquire a small competitor for $2,400,000 in cash, adding $80,000 of MRR.
Raise list prices 15% for NEW customers only (existing customers unchanged).
decisions.objective: Improve unit economics on new business.

stated_assumptions.statement: The effect of the price increase on new-customer conversion rate is not measured; no elasticity data is provided.

decisions.proposal: Accept a new 400-unit order, contractually due in 5 months, on top of the existing 200-unit backlog.
Invest $1,800,000 in capex to expand production capacity from 25 to 60 units/month, with a 4-month ramp (months 1-4 at 25/mo, months 5-6 at 60/mo).
decisions.objective: Meet existing demand and contractual delivery obligations.

stated_assumptions.statement: The capacity ramp completes on the stated schedule.

decisions.proposal: Cut the unit sale price from $9,000 to $6,500 to win a price-sensitive segment. Assume this doubles order volume.

stated_assumptions.statement: The price cut doubles order volume.

decisions.proposal: Launch a new premium SKU at 35% contribution margin. Launch cost $1,500,000; projected incremental revenue $600,000/mo.

stated_assumptions.statement: The $600,000/mo is incremental; the degree to which it draws sales away from the existing premium Line A is not specified.

decisions.proposal: Increase Line B marketing spend by $400,000/mo to grow value-segment share.
Discontinue Line B entirely and reallocate its resources to Line A.
decisions.objective: Concentrate the business on the higher-margin line.

stated_assumptions.statement: The incremental return Line A would generate from the reallocated resources is not quantified.

decisions.proposal: Invest $200,000 in a customer-success program projected to cut monthly churn from 2.5% to 2.0%.

stated_assumptions.statement: Comparable customer-success programs at similar-stage companies have reduced churn by 15-25%.

decisions.proposal: Renegotiate the Line A supplier contract for a 2-percentage-point reduction in Line A COGS, at no cost. The supplier has verbally agreed.

stated_assumptions.statement: The supplier has verbally agreed; the deal is not yet signed (execution risk).
